author: Teresa Elena Frontado,Igor Patrick
description:
China pledged on Wednesday to stand by Cuba against sanctions and foreign interference, days after Washington penalised two Chinese state-linked firms for allegedly supplying the Cuban military.
Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Cuban counterpart Bruno Rodriguez in Beijing that China would firmly support Cuba in safeguarding its sovereignty and opposing sanctions, blockades and foreign interference, regardless of how the international situation changed.
The ministry’s readout said Rodriguez...
title: China backs Cuba as Havana raises US fuel pressure in Beijing

author: Brian Y. S. Wong
description:
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is set to take place in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Shenzhen will also be playing host to the first of two further meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump this year.
When the two leaders met in May and September, they called for “constructive strategic stability” as a prescription for US-China relations. Both sides are keen to maintain the fragile detente, in part due to domestic considerations.
Beijing wants to...
title: Low-hanging fruit for Xi and Trump to pluck at Shenzhen Apec summit

author: Igor Patrick,Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Florida’s attorney general has issued an investigative subpoena to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) to determine whether the group accepted money or other support from the Chinese and Cuban governments.
Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the move in a video posted on social media on Tuesday, saying his office wanted to establish whether the organisation “accepted contributions or support from foreign sources of concern, including the regimes in Cuba and China”, and whether its...
title: Did China and Cuba fund US socialists? Florida’s attorney general demands answers

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a phone call with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday to finalise preparations for next week’s meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China.
“The two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-US relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a right approach for the two countries to get along with each other,” Chinese state news agency Xinhua quoted Wang as...
title: Rubio, Wang hold phone call before Xi-Trump meeting next week

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China’s infantry units are adapting to the growing threat from drones, with some brigades introducing compulsory counter-drone training, new equipment and fresh tactics to help soldiers evade aerial surveillance and attacks.
The latest example comes from a brigade of the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) 75th Group Army, which has made counter-drone training compulsory after an exercise exposed how troops relying on traditional camouflage were vulnerable to drone-directed artillery...
title: How are Chinese infantry units training to survive drone-filled battlefields?

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
A mainland Chinese tourist was asked to sign a declaration recognising Taiwan as an independent state to obtain an entry permit for the island, sparking controversy over Taipei’s entry requirements.
Beijing condemned the demand on Wednesday, accusing Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) of imposing politically motivated restrictions to obstruct cross-strait tourism and exchanges.
“The DPP authorities stubbornly cling to their separatist stance on Taiwan independence and have...
title: Outcry after Taiwan asks mainland Chinese tourist to sign independence statement

author: Fan Chen
description:
Iran has again pointed out the potential role of China in ending its “neither war nor peace” impasse with the United States and pledged concrete steps to deepen ties with Beijing ahead of an expected in-person meeting between Chinese and American leaders next week.
Tehran has underscored its growing reliance on Beijing as Washington doubles down on economic sanctions, according to experts who note that China’s role is, and will remain, significant in regional diplomacy.
Iran’s parliament speaker...
title: Can China help ‘neither war nor peace’ deadlock in Iran before Xi-Trump summit?

author: Ling Xin
description:
A top Chinese-American biologist who left Harvard University to take up a position in China is facing an online backlash amid a growing debate over whether senior returnees are squeezing out the country’s young scientists.
Yuan Junying, a pioneer in the study of how cells die, drew attention in China late last month when she defended her US citizenship after winning a major science prize at the World Laureates Forum in her hometown of Shanghai.
“I’ve always said my blood is Chinese blood,” said...
title: US citizen, ‘Chinese blood’: top biologist Yuan Junying caught in debate over returnees

author: Caroline Lin
description:
India has reportedly formed specialised commando units to patrol its disputed border with China in a bid to claw back its lost tactical edge.
The move is expected to spur Beijing to step up its efforts to improve its infrastructure and force projection in the region.
The units, known as Shaurya platoons, will form part of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police force that patrols the 3,000km (1,865-mile) frontier with Tibet, according to Indian media reports.
The platoons have been given specialised...
title: India forms specialist police commando units to patrol disputed border with China

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage of Jensen Huang’s affair and its potential repercussions. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Could Jensen Huang’s affair become another ‘spy balloon’ saga for US-China ties?
China hawks in Washington could weaponise allegations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence, despite denials from Beijing, Chinese experts warn.
2. ‘Adding fuel to fire’: how Nvidia CEO’s troubles could...
title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair: everything you need to know

author: Liu Zhen
description:
One year after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s remarks on a Taiwan contingency froze Beijing-Tokyo ties, a Japanese media report has detailed a failed diplomatic mission to turn the table.
The episode, revealed by the Yomiuri newspaper on Sunday, occurred during a meeting in Beijing on November 18 last year between Masaaki Kanai from the Japanese foreign ministry and his Chinese counterpart Liu Jinsong, then head of Asian affairs.
The report said Kanai was conveying a message from Takaichi that...
title: How China’s 2-for-1 diplomatic threat forced Japan’s Takaichi to back down

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a more balanced trade relationship with China, with the objective to “de-risk, not decouple”, as Chinese ambassador Xie Feng spoke of adhering to “red lines” at an event in New York on Tuesday.
“Trade must advance the interests of both parties without diminishing the sovereignty of either,” said Bessent, while emphasising that US-China ties were defined by the relationship between their leaders, who are due to meet next week for a summit.
“That...
title: Bessent urges US, China to ‘de-risk, not decouple’ as Xie points to ‘red lines’

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China has established an institute dedicated to preserving rare and endangered historical disciplines, advancing Beijing’s push to elevate traditional culture as a pillar of its soft power and national narrative.
The institute was inaugurated at the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (UCASS) in Beijing on Friday, alongside the launch of an association to consolidate nationwide resources involving the studies.
The institute includes a dozen ancient ethnic minority scripts such as...
title: Written in bone: China bets on ancient scripts for modern soft power

author: Nayan Seth
description:
During a video call on Friday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng to uphold China’s previous commitments on agricultural goods and rare earth exports.
A day earlier, Beijing reminded Washington to implement another deal – reciprocal tariff cuts covering US$30 billion worth of products on each side – as a precondition to buying more American farm products.
Just days before President Donald Trump meets Chinese leader Xi...
title: Deal vs deal? US, China trade calls to honour commitments before Xi-Trump summit

author: Khushboo Razdan,Nayan Seth,Dewey Sim,William Zheng
description:
Talks between China, the US and Russia could yield a commitment to control AI in nuclear arsenals as part of a broader agenda on global governance, sources told the South China Morning Post.
The three nations have engaged in weeks of back-and-forth discussion to nail down the agenda and protocol for talks between the countries’ leaders on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen next week.
The sources said that the war in Ukraine and denuclearisation of the Korean peninsula had largely...
title: China, Russia and US try to nail down AI nuclear agenda in time for Apec talks
